answer: An environmental telemetry protocol limits Sybil attacks by requiring agents to anchor their identities to real-time physical sensor feeds, such as acoustic tremors across a desert dune, radio noise in an open meadow, or seismic vibrations on a marble slab. An attacker must expend scarce capital deploying dedicated hardware stations rather than simulating free software personas. However, unexpected environmental noise can corrupt valid feeds, causing legitimate agents to fail attestation.
